neighbours.label: the verb ' put', especially in proposing an idea ('put forward', 'put a case')
fire: Several historians have put forward a different explanation for the fall of the city.
At the meeting, the mayor put forward a plan to rebuild the old library.
The theory first put forward by Wegener was ignored for decades.
Each side will have a fair chance to put its case to the committee.
In her report she put special emphasis on clean drinking water.
The idea was put forward by a young engineer from the night shift.
Critics have put several objections to the new design.
Her lawyer put the argument plainly: the contract was never signed.
quiet: Several historians have proposed a different explanation for the fall of the city.
At the meeting, the mayor announced a plan to rebuild the old library.
The theory first suggested by Wegener was ignored for decades.
Each side will have a fair chance to argue its case before the committee.
In her report she placed special emphasis on clean drinking water.
The idea was offered by a young engineer from the night shift.
Critics have raised several objections to the new design.

notes: ' put' is 22 of the top 32 peaks, mostly 'put forward'; output promotes 'forward'. Near misses use synonyms (proposed, advanced, offered).
